chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of vinegar according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies vinegar as a substance that strengthens the intellect, reflecting the broader Shia tradition of linking dietary habits to spiritual and cognitive clarity. This statement is often interpreted not merely as a physiological effect but as a means to enhance focus and wisdom, aligning with the Islamic emphasis on maintaining a sound mind for worship and reflection.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Suleyman Bin Khalid, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Vinegar strengthens the power of understanding.’”
